summary:
AgroVision – Project Brief

"AgroVision" is an AI-powered, data-driven agricultural decision-support platform designed to help smallholder farmers adapt to changing climate conditions and make smarter farming decisions.

By integrating real-time and historical environmental data from NASA APIs, particularly NASA POWER, AgroVision analyzes critical agricultural parameters such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, and soil moisture for a farmer's specific location. Farmers can select their farm location, provide their month-wise crop rotation details, and receive localized insights into environmental conditions and potential agricultural risks.

The platform combines NASA Earth observation data, farmer-provided information, and AI-powered analysis to generate personalized crop suitability assessments, climate risk alerts, and actionable farming recommendations.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between space-based scientific data and ground-level agriculture, empowering farmers with accessible, location-specific insights to build more resilient, sustainable, and climate-smart farming systems.
details:
AgroVision is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers make informed farming decisions using NASA satellite and environmental data. It collects location-specific climate information, including temperature, rainfall, humidity, and soil moisture, through NASA POWER APIs. Farmers can select their farm location and enter monthly crop rotation details to receive AI-generated crop suitability assessments, climate risk insights, and personalized farming recommendations.

The project benefits smallholder farmers by making complex scientific data accessible and practical, helping reduce climate-related agricultural risks, improve crop planning, and promote sustainable farming. Our intended impact is to build climate-resilient agriculture, particularly in rural communities.

We developed AgroVision using React.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, and AI integration with Gemini. We also used NASA POWER APIs, Leaflet, and OpenStreetMap.

Our creativity lies in combining space-based environmental data, local farming practices, and AI into one accessible platform. We considered farmers' accessibility, regional climate variations, crop rotation patterns, data reliability, usability, and affordability while designing the solution.
